A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLE-based model-based RL work. Their complete main texts, algorithms, equations, references and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds and proofs, including analytical tabular-MDP examples. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical. Its additional Eluder-dimension analyses and coverage example are mathematical results, not experiments or data analyses.

M1.justification: The matched O-MBRL and CPPO-LR pseudocode retains the same MLE, version-space and planning steps. However, v3 restricts the policy class to deterministic nonstationary policies and introduces a conditional value-range filtering step when bounded model values are not assumed (Section 3, footnote 2).

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or benchmarks. The revised offline data-generation assumptions and tabular examples concern theoretical coverage, not empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. Comparisons with Uehara and Sun (2021), Ren et al. (2021) and other methods concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither PDF contains experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets or testing protocols. Changes to theoretical sampling and coverage assumptions are assessed under T1.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments or empirical case studies. The added appendix analyses establish mathematical lemmas.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical error bars or significance tests. Variances and failure probabilities appear in theoretical guarantees rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No measured scores, rankings or empirical findings appear in either version. The substantially revised analytical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the online distributional Eluder complexity with pointwise state-action Eluder complexity, introduces logarithmic horizon dependence and removes v1's bilinear-class example and claim. Appendices B–D add self-normalization, exceptional-episode and recursive-moment arguments and substantially replace the online proof. Offline analysis replaces population coverage under i.i.d. behavior trajectories with sample-based coverage allowing adaptive collection; Appendix E revises the proof and adds a tabular coverage derivation. v3 also restricts policies to deterministic ones, explicitly bounds model values and restricts Lemma 1's distributions to [0,1].

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the overall guarantee to nearly horizon-free learning. Unlike v1's finite-class online claim without logarithmic horizon dependence and its bilinear-class justification, v3's online guarantee has logarithmic horizon factors under pointwise Eluder assumptions. Completely horizon-free offline learning is retained under a different coverage condition, and the explicit extension to stochastic policies in deterministic systems is removed.

C2.justification: v3 Section 5 explicitly states that its horizon-free offline result does not hold under the earlier population-coverage formulation and leaves that setting open. Section 4.1 also explains why direct Eluder transfer and the expected-error simulation-lemma route are insufficient, motivating the new samplewise and moment-recursion analysis. These substantially revise applicability boundaries and explanations; the concluding limitations paragraph is otherwise retained.

D1.justification: The matched algorithms retain their likelihood thresholds and trajectory-to-transition-tuple construction. Neither version adds implementation resources, hardware, runtime measurements or code/data access information; the procedural refinement is identified under M1.

R1.justification: The relationship to prior theory changes substantively. v3 removes the bilinear-class positioning associated with Du et al. (2021), aligns offline coverage with Ye et al. (2024), and explicitly distinguishes its guarantee from Uehara and Sun's coverage setting. It also positions the online result as obtaining guarantees similar to Huang et al. (2024) through simpler MLE-based algorithms, and adds several supporting references.

P1.justification: The online and offline sections exchange order, and the main proof sketch shifts from offline analysis to a substantially rewritten online argument. The introduction and contribution summary are revised, while the appendices are reorganized around an added roadmap, separate Eluder analysis and reordered proof sections. This changes the document's explanatory structure substantially.

P2.justification: Both retain the same single-column visual style without figures or result tables. The two algorithm boxes exchange positions and numbering, and mathematical displays are reformatted and redistributed with the reorganized sections; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves the theoretical support and qualification of the central claims. It replaces v1's direct population-error and Eluder-transfer arguments with explicit samplewise, exceptional-episode and moment-recursion analyses, and acknowledges that the earlier offline coverage guarantee remains unresolved. The cost is narrower policy/function-class scope and logarithmic online horizon dependence. These qualifications and supporting derivations make the paper substantially more defensible, although some broad wording remains in the unchanged conclusion.
